rejected_videos.reason: Video is entirely a qualitative comparison of mean/median/mode ORDER under right-skew, symmetric, and left-skew shapes (wealth/comment/lifespan examples) -- it never performs an actual mean/median/mode computation from a list of numbers (no sum-and-divide, no middle-value ordering, no frequency count), so it doesn't teach this concept's computation facts (f1-f3). Teaching it here would also mean leaning on stats.distribution_shape's content throughout, which this concept blocks.

Video explains null-hypothesis / fail-to-reject reasoning generically using mean recovery-time comparisons between drugs -- it never uses confidence intervals, never uses the p0=0.333 proportion example, never frames an A/B test's positive/negative/neutral outcome against a baseline, and never raises the large-sample statistical-vs-practical-significance caveat. None of this concept's six required facts (all pinned to specific CI/proportion/A-B-test numbers) appear anywhere in this video.

Video assumes INDEX/MATCH syntax is already known and only debates VLOOKUP-vs-INDEX/MATCH preference on raw lookup-count/performance grounds (an 'interview question' framing); it never states MATCH's or INDEX's syntax (f1/f3), never discusses match_type 0 vs 1 (f2), and frames the INDEX/MATCH advantage as speed on huge datasets rather than VLOOKUP's left-to-right limitation (f4) -- the concept's actual required facts aren't taught here.

Video is entirely about calculating EFFECTIVE sample size when replicates are correlated (biological vs technical replicates, the n/(1+(n-1)r) formula) -- it never addresses why a bigger sample gives a more precise or trustworthy point estimate (f1) or that more cases improve effect-size estimation (f2), which are this concept's actual required facts. The video also explicitly states it builds on a separate prerequisite StatQuest video the learner hasn't been assigned.

Video never uses the terms control, treatment, baseline, or random assignment anywhere in its transcript -- it's a loose, repetitive description of comparing product thumbnails/banners by click-through rate (e-commerce/Netflix/YouTube-ad examples), without the randomized-experiment structure (f1, f2) or the control-vs-variation-vs-baseline framing (f3) this concept requires. Ends with an unrelated sponsor plug.
No transcript file exists for this video (catalogue duration is only 17 seconds), so no range can be proposed or verified.

Video is entirely about calculating Q1/Q3/IQR and the 1.5xIQR lower/upper bracket formula to mechanically flag and remove outliers -- it never reasons about whether an outlier is a data-entry error or a genuine observation, or why a genuine outlier shouldn't be removed without good reason (this concept's actual f1-f3). It also relies on quartiles/IQR, which is blocked knowledge for this concept (viz.box_plots, where IQR is formally taught, is in this concept's blocked_knowledge_ids).

Video never demonstrates PivotTables (f1) -- its 'Excel Tables' chapter (691-811s) is about Ctrl+T structured ranges for dynamic formula references, a different feature entirely, not PivotTable construction (select range, insert PivotTable, drag fields to Rows/Columns/Values). The COUNTIFS content needed for f2 exists elsewhere in this same video but is already proposed under spreadsheet.conditional_aggregation from this source, and nothing here applies these skills to a capstone-style project.
